title: 2007 AMC 10B Problem 12
statement: Tom’s age is \(T\) years, which is also the sum of the ages of his three children. His age \(N\) years ago was twice the sum of their ages then. What is \(\frac{T}{N}?\)

solutions.text:
\(N\) years ago Tom’s age was \(T-N,\) and the sum of his three children’s ages was \(T-3N.\)

The condition gives \(T-N=2(T-3N),\) so \(T-N=2T-6N,\) which simplifies to \(5N=T.\)

Therefore \(\frac{T}{N}=5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Express the children’s total age \(N\) years ago in terms of \(T\) and \(N\)
